canvas-01-1.description: Part 1 of printed sheet 1 is the western edge of Flemington at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned about 26 degrees so that Mine Street and Bonnell Street run across the sheet slightly rising to the right. Bonnell Street crosses the upper half and Mine Street the lower half, joined by Shields on the left of the central block and Dewey Av. on the right, with Shields Court running down the right edge below Mine Street. The central block between Bonnell, Shields, Mine and Dewey Av. is mostly open ground, with a handful of dwellings, an ice house, a corn crib, an auto shed and a cluster of dwellings and a long blue building on narrow lots at its east end. Along Bonnell Street at the top there are dwellings, coops and auto sheds, with part of block 27 above. Mine Brook comes in from the upper left, crosses Mine Street at a plank bridge and continues south, its course lettered along the stream. A pump house with its electric motor lies near the brook, a north arrow points up and to the right, and the borough limits run as a dash-dot line beside Shields. South of Mine Street a few dwellings and farm buildings stand in open fields in block 20. West of the brook, block 33 holds a farmstead with old barns, silos, sheds and a stone dwelling. The index, key map, legend and location map above, and the Fair Grounds inset, are separate and not covered here.
notes: Bonnell is today Bonnell Street; Mine is today Mine Street
Shields is today Shields Avenue
Dewey Av. is lettered on the right edge; sheet 7 continues the same streets to the east
Plank Bridge carries Mine Street over Mine Brook
The borough limits are drawn beside Shields

Printed sheet 1: index, key map (small scale, not used), legend, NJ location map; below them two map parts at 100 ft. Part 1: blocks 20, 21, 27, 33 along Mine Street, Bonnell Street, Shields and Dewey Avenues west of sheet 7, drawn turned about 26 degrees like sheet 7. Part 2: inset of the Flemington Fair Grounds ('located 1 mile N. of P.O.'), Flemington Road, Oak Grove School, race track; own north arrow pointing left; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Flemington Fair Grounds, Flemington Road, Oak Grove School (located 1 mile north of the post office) (no street junction; outside the reference box; needs identify Flemington Road and the fairground site on modern data north of the borough, then parcel corners or a hand-placed anchor (step 6b)).

sheet-2-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 2 is the downtown core of Flemington at 50 feet to an inch. Main Street runs north to south down the middle of the sheet, from the fork at North Main Street and the Branch road at the top, past Pennsylvania Avenue and the Soldiers Monument on a small triangular island, through Capner Street and Bloomfield Avenue, to Court Street at the foot. West of Main Street the sheet shows the Public Park with a bandstand and a compass rose, the County Court House and Jail (drawn in blue) with the Fire Department house and jail yard, county offices, a hotel and its shed, the Palace Theatre, the County Hotel and Pool Room, and a row of stores and dwellings, all between Park Avenue on the west and Main Street. East of Main Street are stores, a bakery, barbers, a confectioner, auto sales, an auto repair shop, a bank and the Union Hotel, Mallory Mfg. Co. and a garage along Bloomfield Avenue, with dwellings and sheds behind, and Spring Street at the lower right edge. The boxed inset at the top left, the Flemington Water Co. reservoirs on Capner Street, is a separate part and is not covered here. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches, fire alarm boxes and hydrants are drawn in the streets. Blocks are numbered 4, 5, 6, 9 and 25, with older numbers in brackets. The sheet carries the Flemington oval title and printed number 2 at the top right, and the neighbouring sheets 3, 5, 6, 7 and 4 are indicated at its edges.
notes: Pennsylvania Av. is also lettered Penn; Pennsylvania Avenue is today Pennsylvania Avenue
The road lettered N. Main St. is today North Main Street
Capner is today Capner Street, Court is today Court Street, Park Av. is today Park Avenue
The Soldiers Monument stands on a triangular island between North Main Street and the Branch road
Borough limits are lettered on the inset line, outside this part
Branch (lettered between the two pipe labels on the diagonal road north-east of the Soldiers Monument) is today East Main Street

Printed sheet 2, 50 ft to an inch. Part 1: downtown, Main Street from Pennsylvania Avenue to Court Street, Capner, Park Avenue, Bloomfield Avenue to Spring Street; Court House and Jail, Union Hotel, Palace Theatre. Part 2: boxed inset top left, Flemington Water Co. reservoirs on Capner Street (own north arrow); no street junction, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Flemington Water Co. reservoirs on Capner Street (no street junction; only the south edge of Capner Street and the borough line are drawn; needs parcel corners of the water company lot or the borough line crossing Capner Street (step 6b)).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Flemington, Hunterdon County, at 50 feet to an inch, from Court Street at the top to William Street near the foot. Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet and Mine Street crosses it diagonally to the south-west. The east side of Main Street is the commercial core: a row of stores (dry goods, jeweler, grocery, bank with a lodge room above, cigars and printing, auto supplies, drugs) between Court Street and Higgins Avenue, then the Methodist Episcopal church with its parsonage, the Public Library, the Post Office with a club room, a hardware and furniture store and more dwellings and stores down to William Street. Spring Street bounds this side on the east. West of Main Street, between Court Street and Mine Street, lie the Flemington Steam Laundry, wagon sheds, liveries, auto garages, an American Legion room and rows of dwellings, with a stone church building drawn in blue. Between Mine Street and Park Avenue the lots run diagonally, and south of Mine Street the Fulper Pottery Co. occupies a large block of kilns, storage and finishing rooms, with a note that a night watchman punches time every hour. The sheet has fire hydrants, telephone and fire alarm boxes, and 6 inch and 8 inch water pipes drawn along the streets. Streets are labelled with house numbers. Blocks are numbered 9, 10, 11, 20 and 24, each with an earlier number in brackets. Blocks on the sheet's lower right and lower left belong to sheets 4 and 7, and a compass rose stands at the top of the sheet.
notes: Higgins Avenue (also lettered Union) is today Chorister Place, a 20 ft street
Bonnell St. at the left edge is today Bonnell Street
Mine is today Mine Street; Court is today Court Street
Park Av. is today Park Avenue and Maple Av. is today Maple Avenue
Fulper Pottery Co. works south of Mine Street
The lettering Higgins Av. (7) (8) carries block numbers in brackets, not alternate names

Printed sheet 3, 50 ft to an inch. Downtown from Court Street to William Street between Park Avenue and Spring Street: Main, Mine, Maple Avenue, Higgins Avenue (Union; today Chorister Place, 20 ft), Fulper Pottery Co., post office, Methodist Episcopal church.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the eastern side of Flemington at 100 feet to an inch, from New York Avenue at the top to Church Street at the foot. Main Street runs down the left edge of the lower half; Spring Street and Broad Street run north to south through the middle, crossed by Bloomfield Avenue, Maple Avenue, William Street and Elwood Avenue on the right. Blocks are numbered 4, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14 and 16, with earlier numbers in brackets. The upper part is mostly dwellings and gardens on large lots, with a garage, the Crescent Garment Co. Inc. fur manufactory with its watchman and fire protection notes, and an opera house marked as damaged by fire along Spring Street. The east side of the sheet is largely open land, with the borough limits drawn as a dash-dot line on the right. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, with several tracks. Along it are the Flemington Cut Glass Co., the Flemington Electric Light Co., Hill Bros. hay, coal and farm implements, the John B. Case Lumber Co. with a long lumber shed, the New Jersey Cider Vinegar Works with tanks, and the Dural Rubber Co. near the right edge. A cemetery and the Baptist Church lie along Main Street at the lower left. A compass rose stands at the left, the scale is lettered at the top and the bottom, and sheets 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 are indicated at the edges.
notes: New York Av. is also lettered Fell; the street is today New York Avenue
Higgins Av. is today Chorister Place
Broad is today Broad Street; Main is today Main Street
Elwood Av. is today Elwood Avenue, Church is today Church Street
Spring is today Spring Street, William is today William Street
Opera House is marked as damaged by fire
Printed scale is 100 ft to an inch

Printed sheet 4, 100 ft. East side: New York Avenue (Fell) to Church Street, Spring, Broad, Elwood Avenue, Maple Avenue, William; Central Railroad of New Jersey; Flemington Cut Glass, J.B. Case lumber, New Jersey Cider Vinegar Works, Dural Rubber, cemetery.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the northern edge of Flemington at 100 feet to an inch. North Main Street (Main) and the Branch road run north-east from the lower left towards the top of the sheet, with Hopewell Avenue closing the triangle between them on the north and Wyckoff Street running off Branch to North Broad Street (Broad). Pennsylvania Avenue (Penn) crosses the foot of the sheet from left to right, with New York Avenue (Fell) at the bottom and Elwood Avenue, marked not opened, running down the right side. The blocks between North Main Street and Branch hold a cemetery with the Presbyterian church (drawn in blue) at its lower end, and dwellings on long narrow lots fill the triangle between Branch and North Broad Street. Industry is at the upper left: the John C. Roche coal yard, John Scott Machine Shop, a feed mill, and the N.J. Northern Gas Co. with its gas holder beside the Lehigh Valley Railroad tracks, which run diagonally across the corner. A brook crosses the upper part of the sheet from the left towards the right, with a smaller stream joining it, and the borough limits are drawn as a dash-dot line. Calvary Episcopal Church stands at the lower centre. The right half of the sheet is largely open land with scattered farm buildings, an auto repair shop on the Branch road and a compass rose. Block numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 30 and 31 appear, some with older numbers in brackets. The scale is lettered twice, at the top and at the foot.
notes: N. Main (Main) is today North Main Street
Branch is today East Main Street
Wyckoff is today New Jersey Avenue
N. Broad (Broad) is today Broad Street
Pennsylvania Av. (Penn) is today Pennsylvania Avenue
New York Av. (Fell) is today New York Avenue
Elwood Av. is lettered Not Opened along its northern stretch
Hopewell Av. is today Hopewell Avenue
The brook is lettered only Brook; it is probably Mine Brook but no name is printed

Printed sheet 5, 100 ft. North side: N. Main (Main), Hopewell Avenue, Branch (today East Main Street), Wyckoff (today New Jersey Avenue), N. Broad (Broad), Pennsylvania Avenue (Penn), Elwood Avenue, New York Avenue (Fell); Presbyterian church, cemetery, Lehigh Valley Railroad, N.J. Northern Gas Co.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the north-western edge of Flemington at 100 feet to an inch. North Main Street (Main) crosses the upper half from the left edge and bends south-east to meet Main Street at the lower right, where Branch Street and Pennsylvan. Avenue leave towards the east. Allen Street runs down the left side and Park Avenue down the middle, with Corcoran Street, a narrow 20 foot street, crossing between them and Capner Street running along the lower edge. Most of the sheet is open farmland and large undivided lots, with scattered farm buildings along the top and left. The industrial buildings are concentrated beside the Lehigh Valley Railroad, which comes in from the upper right with its tracks fanning into sidings: the Empire Cut Glass Co. cutting and polishing works, Alvin Hill and Son feed, flour and grain mill with a railroad spur, the Flemington Dairy Association, and the engine house and coal shed. Pedrick's Brick Yard, not in operation, with drying racks and kilns, stands at the left. Hopewell Avenue appears at the right, next to a row of dwellings along North Main Street and a long frame building. Blocks are numbered 26 to 32, some with older numbers in brackets, and sheets 2, 5 and 7 are indicated at the edges. The borough limits run as a dash-dot line at the upper right. A compass rose is at the right and the scale is lettered at the top and the foot.
notes: N. Main (Main) is today North Main Street; Main is today Main Street
Branch St. is today East Main Street
Printed abbreviated as Pennsylvan. Av.; the street is today Pennsylvania Avenue
Corcoran is today Corcoran Street (drawn about 20 ft wide)
Allen is today Allen Street; Park Av. is today Park Avenue; Capner is today Capner Street
Hopewell Av. is today Hopewell Avenue
Pedrick's Brick Yard is marked not in operation
Printed sheet 6, 100 ft. North-west: N. Main (Main), Allen, Park Avenue, Corcoran (drawn 20 ft), Capner; Lehigh Valley Railroad depot and yard, Empire Cut Glass Co., Pedrick's brick yard.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the western side of Flemington at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned about 25 degrees so that Bonnell Street and Mine Street run across the sheet nearly horizontally and Park Avenue and Main Street run up the right side. Allen Street and Court Street (Stryker Av.) descend from the upper centre towards Park Avenue. Dewey Avenue is at the left edge, Academy Street runs between Bonnell and Mine Streets, and Lloyd Pl. and Church Street are in the lower half. The upper part holds a public school and the Public High School standing in open ground, a grand stand and a few outbuildings; the blocks between Bonnell and Mine Streets are filled with dwellings on narrow lots, and the blocks east of Academy Street hold dwellings, the Bodine Lumber Co. beside the railroad, and a few shops. The lower centre is railroad ground: the Pennsylvania Railroad yard and freight station running up the sheet and the Central Railroad of New Jersey curving across the lower part with a turntable, together with the John C. Roche Coal Yard No. 1 with its coal pockets, the engine house, and the Flemington Milling Co. feed, flour and grain mill with its watchman and fire protection notes. Along the lower right edge Main Street is lined with dwellings and a depot. Block numbers 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 20, 22, 23, 26 and 27 appear, some with older numbers in brackets. A compass rose stands at the right and the scale is lettered at the top and the foot. The title oval of the sheet is at the upper right.
notes: Court (Stryker Av.) is today Court Street
Bonnell is today Bonnell Street; Mine is today Mine Street
Lloyd Pl. is today Lloyd Avenue
Allen is today Allen Street; Park Av. is today Park Avenue; Capner is today Capner Street
Brown St. is today Brown Street; Church is today Church Street
Sheet is drawn turned about 25 degrees from north

Printed sheet 7, 100 ft, drawn turned about 25 degrees. West side: Bonnell, Mine, Dewey Avenue, Academy, Lloyd Place, Court (Stryker Avenue), Allen, Park Avenue, Church; public school, Bodine Lumber Co., Pennsylvania Railroad and Central Railroad of New Jersey yards, J.C. Roche coal yard.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the southern part of Flemington at 100 feet to an inch, from Church Street at the top to the open country south of the borough limits. Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet and swings south-west at the foot of the built-up area, where Reaville Rd. branches off to the south-east. Brown Street runs south from Church Street on the left of the built-up blocks, with Grant Street and Parker Av. crossing it, and Broad is lettered at the top right edge. The upper part holds dwellings on regular lots between Church Street, Brown Street and Main Street, with a few auto sheds, a school and Smith's Garage drawn in blue. The industrial area is at the left: the Foran Foundry and Mfg. Co. with its foundry, pattern shop, cleaning sheds, machine shops, storage and the watchman, fire pail and hydrant notes, Higgins Bros. coal, hay and straw, and a turn table with an engine house beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks that run up the left edge. The lower half has almost no streets other than Main Street and Reaville Rd.; it shows scattered farm buildings, a slaughter house and open fields, with the borough limits drawn as a dash-dot line across the sheet. Block numbers 15, 17, 18, 19 and 20 appear, some with older numbers in brackets, and neighbouring sheets 4 and 7 are indicated at the top. A compass rose is at the right and the scale is lettered at the top and the foot. The title oval is at the upper right.
notes: Church is today Church Street; Brown is today Brown Street
Grant is today Grant Avenue
Reaville Rd. is today Reaville Avenue
Parker Av. is today Parker Avenue
Main is today Main Street; Broad is today Broad Street
Borough limits run across the lower half of the sheet
Foran Foundry and Mfg. Co. and a turn table stand beside the railroad at the left

Printed sheet 8, 100 ft. South: Church Street to the borough limits, Brown, Grant, Main, Parker Avenue, Reaville Road; Foran Foundry & Mfg. Co., Pennsylvania Railroad turntable, Smith's Garage. Lower half has no surviving junction (Main / Reaville fork rebuilt).
